name: workflow_create
description:
Create a new workflow as a JSON graph of nodes and edges.

Call workflow_list first to check that the id you choose does not already exist.
Call workflow_node_catalog to discover supported node types before authoring nodes.
Call tool_list/tool_get to discover valid action_id values before authoring tool nodes; do not guess tool names. For example, the live web search action in this registry is currently `websearch`, not `web_search`.

When using tool nodes, pass only parameters required for the behavior. Do not add optional typed tool parameters just because the direct tool supports them; workflow runners and template interpolation can coerce values differently from direct tool calls, especially inside for_each/subworkflows. Prefer known working minimal parameter shapes and tool defaults unless the optional parameter is necessary and has been tested in workflow execution.

Avoid workflow tool nodes for tools that require deeply nested object/array parameters unless verified in an actual workflow run. Current runners may stringify nested arrays/objects (for example `question.questions` may become `[object Object]`). For human-in-the-loop workflows, prefer: workflow outputs machine-readable options -> parent/session calls `question` directly -> follow-up deterministic step consumes selected labels.

## WORKFLOW TOP-LEVEL FIELDS

  id          – unique kebab-case identifier, e.g. "research-report"
  name        – human-readable display name
  description – what this workflow does (optional)
  version     – semver string, defaults to "1.0.0" (optional)
  nodes       – array of WorkflowNode objects
  edges       – array of directed connections between nodes

## NODE SHAPE (every node)

  {
    "id":       "unique-node-id",
    "type":     "workflow",
    "data":     { ... },              ← node-type-specific (see below)
    "position": {"x": 0, "y": 0}     ← layout hint; increment y by 150 per step
  }

## NODE TYPES AND THEIR data SHAPES

### 1. parameters  — workflow inputs; must be the root node (no inbound edges)

  "data": {
    "nodeType": "parameters",
    "node": {"label": "Parameters"},
    "workflowParameters": [
      {"name": "topic",  "type": "string",  "description": "Topic to research",                     "required": true},
      {"name": "mode",   "type": "string",  "description": "Processing mode", "required": true, "enum": ["fast", "thorough"]},
      {"name": "count",  "type": "number",  "description": "How many items to return",              "required": false},
      {"name": "enabled","type": "boolean", "description": "Enable extra processing",              "required": false}
    ]
  }

  workflowParameters fields:
    name        – parameter name, used as the $input.<name> reference key (required)
    type        – one of: string, number, integer, boolean, object, array (required)
    description – shown to the LLM and in the run dialog to guide the caller (required)
    required    – true if the caller must provide a value; false if optional (required)
    enum        – array of allowed values when the input is constrained.

  • Values passed to workflow_run as `input` are mapped by name to these parameters.
  • All parameter values become available downstream as $input.<name>.
  • Always include a parameters node when the workflow takes any inputs.

### 2. prompt  — ask the session agent to reason, write, or analyse; capture its reply

  "data": {
    "nodeType": "prompt",
    "instructions": "Analyse the following about \"$input.topic\":\n\n$ctx.search_results",
    "node": {
      "label": "Analyse Results",
      "parameters": {"output": "analysis"}
    }
  }

  • instructions supports $input.<name> and $ctx.<name> template interpolation.
  • output makes the result accessible as $ctx.<key> in all downstream nodes.
  • Use prompt for open-ended reasoning, writing, analysis, synthesis, or planning.

### 3. structured  — ask the agent to return a validated JSON object matching a schema

  "data": {
    "nodeType": "structured",
    "instructions": "Analyse \"$input.text\" and list all delegations.",
    "outputSchema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "delegations": {
          "type": "array",
          "description": "Top-level delegations found in the text",
          "items": {"type": "object", "properties": {"title": {"type": "string", "description": "Delegation title"}}, "required": ["title"]}
        }
      },
      "required": ["delegations"]
    },
    "node": {"label": "Extract Delegations", "parameters": {"output": "delegations"}}
  }

  • The agent is forced via tool-calling to return exactly this shape (retried up to 2×).
  • output stores the parsed result in ctx.

### 4. tool  — call a registered tool deterministically

  "data": {
    "nodeType": "tool",
    "node": {
      "label":     "Web Search",
      "action_id": "websearch",       ← verify with tool_list/tool_get before use
      "parameters": {
        "query":  "$input.topic",
        "output": "search_results"
      }
    },
    "agentArgs": []
  }

  • Every key in parameters except "output" is passed as a tool argument.
  • $input.* and $ctx.* are resolved before the tool is called.
  • output stores the tool result in ctx.
  • Keep tool-node parameters minimal. Optional typed parameters may be rejected at runtime if the workflow runner serializes them differently than direct tool calls.

### 5. decide  — branch on an agent choice or a deterministic condition

  Agent mode:
  "parameters": {"mode": "agent", "cases": [{"label": "approved"}, {"label": "needs_revision"}], "default": "needs_revision", "output": "decision"}

  Deterministic mode:
  "parameters": {"mode": "deterministic", "input": "$ctx.score", "cases": [{"label": "high", "when": {"op": "gte", "value": 8}}], "default": "medium"}

  Supported ops: equals, not_equals, in, not_in, contains, not_contains,
                 matches, not_matches, gt, gte, lt, lte,
                 exists, not_exists, is_empty, is_not_empty

## EDGE RULES

  Regular sequential edge:
    {"id": "e1", "source": "node-a", "target": "node-b"}

  Decide node edges:
    • No label or label "result" fires after any decision
    • label = "<case-label>" fires only when that case was chosen
    • label = "else" fires when no labeled case edge matched

## VARIABLE REFERENCES

  $input.<name>   – workflow input parameter
  $ctx.<name>     – stored output of a previous node
  $output.<name>  – alias for $ctx.<name>

## DESIGN GUIDELINES

  1. Start with a parameters node when the workflow takes inputs.
  2. Use prompt nodes for reasoning, writing, analysis, and synthesis.
  3. Use tool nodes for deterministic I/O; verify action_id names with tool_list/tool_get.
  4. Use decide nodes for routing.
  5. Name output keys semantically and store intermediate results explicitly.
  6. For updates to existing workflows, preserve known-working nodes unless the requested change explicitly requires replacing them.

## COMPLETE EXAMPLE — research-report workflow

  {
    "id": "research-report",
    "name": "Research and Report",
    "description": "Search the web, analyse findings, write a structured report",
    "nodes": [
      {"id": "params", "type": "workflow", "data": {"nodeType": "parameters", "node": {"label": "Parameters"}, "workflowParameters": [{"name": "topic", "type": "string", "description": "Topic to research", "required": true}]}, "position": {"x": 0, "y": 0}},
      {"id": "search", "type": "workflow", "data": {"nodeType": "tool", "node": {"label": "Web Search", "action_id": "websearch", "parameters": {"query": "$input.topic", "output": "search_results"}}, "agentArgs": []}, "position": {"x": 0, "y": 150}},
      {"id": "analyse", "type": "workflow", "data": {"nodeType": "prompt", "instructions": "Analyse these search results about \"$input.topic\":\n\n$ctx.search_results", "node": {"label": "Analyse Results", "parameters": {"output": "analysis"}}}, "position": {"x": 0, "y": 300}}
    ],
    "edges": [{"id": "e1", "source": "params", "target": "search"}, {"id": "e2", "source": "search", "target": "analyse"}]
  }

workflow.description: Complete workflow JSON. See the tool description for schema examples; call workflow_node_catalog for live node types and tool_list/tool_get for valid tool-node action_id values before authoring tool nodes. Keep tool-node parameters minimal and prefer proven working parameter shapes; do not add optional typed parameters unless required and workflow-tested.
